stories.title: Bank of Canada governor warns of second‑round oil‑linked inflation in 2027
stories.summary: In a speech to the Economic Club of Canada in Toronto, Governor Tiff Macklem said that despite recent declines in benchmark oil prices, high energy costs will keep pressuring consumers at the pump and beyond in 2027. He warned that a second‑round effect of the recent Middle‑East‑linked oil shock will add to inflation persistence and noted the bank is bracing for larger and more frequent supply shocks.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.
stories.previousTitle: Bank of Canada governor says oil‑linked inflation may return in 2027
stories.previousSummary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem told the Economic Club of Canada that a second‑round effect from the recent oil price shock tied to the Middle‑East conflict is expected to add to inflation persistence in 2027, even though benchmark oil prices have fallen from recent peaks. He said businesses have largely absorbed higher production and transportation costs so far, but historical lags and business‑survey data indicate further cost pass‑through to consumers next year.

stories.title: Russian government data shows over 490,000 military deaths since 2022
stories.summary: At least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the 2022 invasion, according to leaked Rosstat records analysed by the BBC. The data, covering 2021‑September 2026, were obtained after a hack by Belarusian group Cyber Partisans BY and Ukraine’s Silent Crow; BBC Russian and Mediazona matched about 90 % of the entries to open‑source casualty lists. Russia’s statistics agency confirmed the cyber‑attack but said no protected information was leaked.
stories.why: It quantifies the human cost of the war and challenges official claims of a brief conflict.

stories.title: Land mine casualties soar in Syria, two years after war
stories.summary: Sign In Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Eleven-year-old Alaa was tending her family's goats with her siblings in a field behind their home in Umm Khuzaym, north-west Syria, on Sunday when there was a flash and a deafening bang. The incident and others this week bring to nearly 1,000 the number of children killed or injured by explosive ordnance in Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024, according to the UN Mine Action Service (Unmas).

stories.title: Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
stories.summary: Nato chief Mark Rutte and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz respond to reports of Russian plans to launch nuclear weapons into space Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after German reports that Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media.
stories.why: This matters because it could affect economic conditions, trade, technology, public systems or international decisions.
stories.previousTitle: NATO chief says alliance will counter any space threats after reports of Russian nuclear‑armed satellite
stories.previousSummary: NATO Secretary‑General Mark Rutte said the alliance will defend against any threats in space following German media reports that Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear‑armed satellite within 60 days. Intelligence about the possible launch was shared among NATO members earlier this month, though the source of the reports was not identified. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the reports shocking, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismissed the stories as unverified.

stories.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
stories.summary: Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.
